beliefs.practice: Store the DocumentDB/Mongo connection string and any DB credentials only in environment variables or a managed secret store (Azure Key Vault); never hard-code or commit them to the repository or test fixtures.

Retrieve DB credentials at runtime from Azure Key Vault (or another managed secret store) and grant the app principal least-privilege access to the secret instead of embedding passwords in CI or code.
Require TLS/SSL for connections (use the connection string option tls=true/ssl=true) and enforce certificate validation; ensure client drivers are configured to refuse insecure connections.
Create a single shared Motor/MongoClient instance at application startup and reuse it for all operations; do not open a new client per request or per operation.

Tune the driver's connection pool settings (e.g., maxPoolSize/minPoolSize, serverSelectionTimeoutMS, connectTimeoutMS) appropriate to the workload and set them explicitly in the connection URI or client options.

Implement robust retry/backoff logic for transient failures and rate-limited responses: detect HTTP 429 or the driver's equivalent, respect the Retry-After header, and use exponential backoff with jitter for retries.

Provision collection throughput (RU/s) or autoscale appropriately for the de-identification pipeline's read/write pattern; benchmark and raise RUs or enable autoscale to avoid frequent throttling during batch runs.

Design partition keys to evenly distribute data and avoid cross-partition hot spots — pick a high-cardinality field used in query filters (e.g., patientId or sourceId) rather than _id or a low-cardinality constant.

Create explicit indexes on all fields the app queries frequently (for example: sourceId, deid_status, createdAt); use compound indexes where queries filter multiple fields, and add unique indexes when you must prevent duplicates (e.g., unique index on DeidNote.sourceId).

For derived/documented status checks (hasBeenDeid, deidVersion, deidTimestamp) keep small indexed fields to allow efficient lookups for unprocessed notes and to support idempotent pipelines (e.g., index deid_status + sourceId).

Enforce schema/field constraints at the application or DB layer (Beanie model validation, Mongo schema validation) so RawNote always has the fields required for de-identification (sourceId/patientId, text, createdAt) and DeidNote always references sourceId and deid metadata.

Make the de-identification pipeline idempotent: mark notes as processed, use a unique index on DeidNote.sourceId (or use findOneAndUpdate with upsert=false and a filter that checks a processed flag) so repeated runs don't create duplicates.

Avoid storing large clinical blobs directly in documents; if notes or attachments can be very large, store them in Azure Blob Storage and reference them from the document to stay within document-size limits and reduce RU cost.
Do not log PHI (raw text) or DB connection strings; redact or hash identifiers in application logs and ensure CI tests and local dry-runs use synthetic data only.

Before sending clinical text to external LLM services, verify compliance and minimize PHI exposure (use on-prem or contractual protections like a BAA); where possible, perform local regex/tokenization pre-filtering and only send minimal context needed for de-identification.

When using vector search, store vectors as fixed-length float arrays and create a vector index configured for the use-case: set dimension to vector length, choose similarity (cosine/inner_product), and configure HNSW params (m, efConstruction) and runtime ef for latency/recall tradeoffs.

Monitor query RU charge and latency (via driver command monitoring or Azure Monitor/Diagnostic settings); add alerts for sustained high RU consumption or frequent 429s and capture slow query patterns to optimize indexes/queries.

Create indexes in a controlled manner (during deployment or a maintenance window) and avoid unbounded automatic index creation in hot workloads; prefer explicit create_indexes calls in scripts so you can tune index options (sparse/partial, TTL for ephemeral docs).

Handle partial failures and multi-document workflows carefully: use 'at-least-once' semantics with idempotency keys (sourceId + deidVersion) and compensating actions rather than assuming multi-document transactions will always be available or cheap across partitions.

Run automated tests against a dedicated test database or a local emulator (if available) and ensure seed scripts are idempotent and cleaned up after tests; never run tests that modify production collections.
